chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Bashir al-Nabbal, who said:

I went out with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) until we reached Al-Shajara. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Nabbal!' I said, 'At your service.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not obligatory upon anyone from the people of this camp to pray four [rak'at] except me and you, and that is because the time for prayer entered before we went out.'
ai.seo_question: When does the obligation to pray four rak'at fully begin for travelers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the foundational Shia principle that the obligation to pray full (four rak'at) or shortened (two rak'at) prayer is determined by the timing of the prayer's entry relative to the commencement of travel. It highlights the specific exception for the Imam and his companion, illustrating the scholarly distinction between the general rule for travelers and the status of the Imam, who remains in a state of complete prayer even while traveling. This ruling underscores the importance of precise temporal markers in determining ritual obligations within Shia fiqh.
